analysis.note: A feminine nominative singular adjective qualifying buddhiḥ; final member is the PPP vipratipanna from vi-prati-√pad. The later Pāṇinian verifier reported tool_error/unsupported relation for this compound rather than an alternate derivation; I retain the analysis because the bhāṣya explicitly supplies the instrumental vigraha.

verification.detail: compound stem śruti-vipratipanna as Stri/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Genitive singular, glossed by the bhāṣya as tava. Linga is supplied as Pum for the male addressee Arjuna; the form te itself is not overtly gender-distinct.
Feminine nominative singular adjective qualifying buddhiḥ; glossed as free from the motion of distraction.
Locative singular; Śaṅkara here explains samādhi as ātmā, ‘the Self’.
Feminine nominative singular adjective qualifying buddhiḥ; distinguished by the bhāṣya as absence of vikalpa there too.
Subject of sthāsyati; glossed as antaḥkaraṇa, the inner organ.
Accusative singular object of avāpsyasi; glossed by Śaṅkara as viveka-prajñā and samādhi.
The unit prints avāpsyasyi, but the grammatical form is avāpsyasi, supported by the bhāṣya’s avāpsyasi/prāpsyasi.

justifications.decision: The bhāṣya explains the first member by instrumental plurals śrutibhiḥ śravaṇaiḥ and glosses vipratipannā as vikṣiptā satī. The line’s headword śruti-vipratinnā and nānā-pratinnā appear to be plaintext corruptions; the decision does not adopt those spellings.
justifications.chosen: śruti-vipratipannā is an instrumental tatpuruṣa: ‘distracted/confounded by śrutis/hearings,’ not ‘opposed to scripture.’

evidence.quote: śruti-vipratinnā aneka-sādhya-sādhana-saṃbandha-prakāśana-śrutibhiḥ śravaṇaiḥ pravṛtti-nivṛtti-lakṣaṇaiḥ vipratipannā nānā-pratinnā vikṣiptā satī te tava buddhir
evidence.translation: ‘śruti-vipratipannā’: by śrutis/hearings that reveal many relations of ends and means and are characterized by engagement and withdrawal; being vipratipannā, scattered; your buddhi.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara explicitly glosses te by tava and identifies buddhi as the item under discussion; therefore the phrase is ‘your buddhi/understanding.’ The gender value for te is not overt in the form and is supplied only to complete the nominal feature set.
options_considered: buddhiḥ as ordinary intellect without the commentarial antaḥkaraṇa sense
justifications.chosen: te is genitive singular, ‘your,’ with Pum recorded for the male addressee; buddhiḥ is the subject.

evidence.translation: te means tava, ‘your’; buddhi is the subject.

justifications.decision: The bhāṣya glosses sthāsyati as sthirībhūtā bhaviṣyati and niścalā as vikṣepa-calana-varjitā, so the steadiness is specifically freedom from scattering/agitation.
options_considered: niścalā as only a redundant synonym of acalā
niścalā as freedom from distracting movement
justifications.chosen: sthāsyati niścalā means ‘will stand, having become steady, free from the motion of distraction.’

evidence.quote: yadā yasmin kāle sthāsyati sthirībhūtā bhaviṣyati niścalā vikṣepa-calana-varjitā satī
evidence.translation: When, at which time, it will stand—will have become steady; motionless, being free from the motion of distraction.

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara derives samādhi as that in which the mind is placed and then states that this samādhi is the Self; the locative therefore means ‘in that Self.’
options_considered: samādhau as ‘in mental concentration’ without specifying its locus
samādhau as ‘in the Self,’ following Śaṅkara
justifications.chosen: samādhau is construed as ‘in samādhi, i.e. in the Self (ātman).’

evidence.quote: samādhau, samādhīyate cittam asminn iti samādhir ātmā, tasmin ātmani ity etat |
evidence.translation: In samādhi: ‘that in which the mind is placed’ is samādhi, the Self; that means ‘in that Self.’

justifications.decision: The bhāṣya distinguishes acalā by tatrāpi vikalpa-varjitā, ‘even there devoid of alternatives/conceptual wavering.’
options_considered: acalā as a mere duplicate of niścalā
acalā as absence of vikalpa even in the Self
justifications.chosen: acalā adds ‘there too free from vikalpa,’ not merely a second word for motionless.

evidence.translation: acalā means ‘there too devoid of vikalpa.’

justifications.decision: Śaṅkara explains yogam by viveka-prajñāṃ samādhiṃ and avāpsyasi by prāpsyasi, making the object not generic yoking but the attained state/knowledge.
justifications.chosen: yogam avāpsyasi means ‘you will attain yoga,’ glossed as discriminative insight and samādhi.

evidence.quote: tadā tasmin kāle yogam avāpsyasi viveka-prajñāṃ samādhiṃ prāpsyasi
evidence.translation: Then, at that time, you will attain yoga; you will attain discriminative insight, samādhi.

justifications.decision: The unit’s final avāpsyasyi is treated as a typographical error: it is not the expected 2nd singular future form, while the bhāṣya has avāpsyasi and glosses it with prāpsyasi.
justifications.chosen: Read avāpsyasi, not the printed avāpsyasyi.

evidence.translation: You will attain yoga; you will attain discriminative insight, samādhi.

translation:
When your understanding (buddhi), distracted by scriptural hearings (śruti),
shall stand motionless—free from scattering—in samādhi, that is, in the Self,
there too unmoving, without alternative thought,
then you will attain yoga: discriminative insight (viveka-prajñā), samādhi.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might take śruti-vipratipannā as ‘opposed to the Veda’; Śaṅkara instead makes the intellect scattered by many śrutis/hearings about means and ends.
It might render samādhau only as ‘in trance/concentration’; Śaṅkara explicitly construes it here as ‘in the Self.’
It might flatten niścalā and acalā into two identical adjectives; the bhāṣya distinguishes freedom from distracting motion and freedom from vikalpa.
It might translate yoga generically as ‘union’ or ‘practice’; Śaṅkara glosses it as viveka-prajñā and samādhi.
It might reproduce the final typo avāpsyasyi; the grammatical and commentarial reading is avāpsyasi.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 splits śruti-vipratipannā as śruti_Cp + vipratipannā and gives vipratipad as the lemma; I treat the printed hyphenated expression as one tatpuruṣa compound stem śruti-vipratipanna, feminine nominative singular, because the bhāṣya glosses it by śrutibhiḥ ... vipratipannā qualifying buddhiḥ. The later vidyut verifier reported tool_error/unsupported relation rather than an alternate derivation, so this analysis is retained with note.
ByT5 leaves te only as singular; I specify Pum/Sasthi/Eka. The genitive is fixed by the commentary’s te tava, while Pum is supplied for the male addressee; the form itself is common across genders.
ByT5/local text preserves avāpsyasyi; I correct the verified surface to avāpsyasi, the grammatical 2nd singular future, supported by commentary line 4.
ByT5 gives the verbal lemma avāp; per the instruction to separate upasargas, I analyze it as root āp with prefix ava.
mula: śruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā | samādhāv acalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasyi
